_note: What popular benchmarks measure, as described in the post. Scores are not comparable across rows.

benchmarks.name: MMLU
benchmarks.task: multiple-choice question in economics, anatomy, IT security...
benchmarks.blind_spot: rewards recognition; the overall score hides weak subjects

benchmarks.name: GPQA
benchmarks.task: hard expert question (e.g. chemistry), resistant to simple search
benchmarks.blind_spot: small set; the right letter does not prove the right reasoning
benchmarks.pattern: expert labels for hard, bounded questions

benchmarks.name: HumanEval
benchmarks.task: write a small function from a signature and a docstring
benchmarks.blind_spot: small functions are not work in a real repository

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench
benchmarks.task: a real issue from a repository; produce a fix

benchmarks.name: Chatbot Arena
benchmarks.task: two anonymous answers; a person picks the better one
benchmarks.blind_spot: can reward style and length over truth

benchmarks.name: HELM
benchmarks.task: many scenarios and metrics at once
benchmarks.metric: accuracy, robustness, calibration, fairness, toxicity, efficiency
benchmarks.blind_spot: even a broad suite does not cover every use

benchmarks.name: TruthfulQA
benchmarks.task: a question with a popular misconception built in
benchmarks.blind_spot: covers selected myths, not the product's real factuality
benchmarks.pattern: adversarial questions for known failure modes

benchmarks.name: ARC-AGI
benchmarks.task: infer a rule from a few examples, produce the output grid
benchmarks.blind_spot: one family of reasoning, not product readiness
